newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark roars back after sharp slide.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark roars back after sharp slide.

text.p: The dollar made an impressive, near 200-point recovery against the mark on Tuesday, one day after sliding sharply through key supports to its lowest level in two weeks, technical analysts said.
While technicians said support at 1.7100/20 marks should rebuff any dips, a sustained break above 1.7210 resistance is needed before a retest of last week's three-year 1.7375 high.
The dollar blew through minor resistance to hit a high of 1.7155 marks on Tuesday, a dramatic improvement from Monday's weak performance but still well below the April 15 high.
"It's a brilliant recovery here after breaking 1.70-1.6987 yesterday," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at I.D.E.A.
The 1.70 to 1.6990 band was a psychological barrier and a 50-percent retracement of the dollar's previous rise from 1.6615 to 1.7375 marks in April.
"We're still toppy off of 1.7375...we have to see more clarification above 1.7205/15 to sustain this recovery," he added.
Technicians questioned whether the dollar's rally would be sustained ahead of this Sunday's Group of Seven (G7) meeting and said any pause could bring the rally to a grinding halt.
"The key thing is follow through. We don't want to see the dollar languish here," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America.
"The longest pause should be through tomorrow, but any pullback to 1.7100/20 should hold if we were to sell off again," he added.
Meanwhile, the dollar barely budged against the yen in U.S. trade, despite a bullish technical outlook.
Keeping dollar gains in check were uncertainty surrounding the upcoming G7 gathering and a pullback in mark/yen from a high near 74.00.
Near-term dollar resistance lies at 126.55 yen, with a more formidable barrier located at 127.20 yen, chartists said.
"We broke out of a triangle pattern two weeks ago, we had a flag that we've broken out of today to the upside, and they both target a move to 129 to 130 (yen)," Johnson said.
"But first we have to get above 127.20," he added.
At 1423 EDT/1823 GMT, the dollar rose to 1.7148/58 marks from 1.7065/75 at the U.S. open, but was unchanged at 125.15/25 yen.
